arxiv-2101-01656.title: On perturbations of dynamical semigroups defined by covariant completely positive measures on the semi-axis
arxiv-2101-01656.creator: G.G. Amosov
arxiv-2101-01656.description: Abstract We consider perturbations of dynamical semigroups on the algebra of all bounded operators in a Hilbert space generated by covariant completely positive measures on the semi-axis. The construction is based upon unbounded linear perturbations of generators of the preadjoint semigroups on the space of nuclear operators.

arxiv-2205-09633.title: Deep Generative Survival Analysis: Nonparametric Estimation of Conditional Survival Function
arxiv-2205-09633.creator: Xingyu Zhou ??, Wen Su ??, Changyu Liu ??, Yuling Jiao, Xingqiu Zhao, Jian Huang
arxiv-2205-09633.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xingyu Zhou ??, Wen Su ??, Changyu Liu ??, Yuling Jiao, Xingqiu Zhao, Jian Huang. We propose a deep generative approach to nonparametric estimation of conditional survival and hazard functions with right-censored data. The key idea of the proposed method is to first learn a conditional generator for the joint conditional distribution of the observed time and censoring indicator given the covariates, and then construct the Kaplan-Meier and Nelson-Aalen estimators based on this conditional generator for the conditional hazard and survival functions.

arxiv-2305-12971.title: Neural Cellular Automata Can Respond to Signals
arxiv-2305-12971.creator: James Stovold
arxiv-2305-12971.description: Abstract Neural Cellular Automata (NCAs) are a model of morphogenesis, capable of growing two-dimensional artificial organisms from a single seed cell. In this paper, we show that NCAs can be trained to respond to signals. Two types of signal are used: internal (genomically-coded) signals, and external (environmental) signals. Signals are presented to a single pixel for a single timestep.

arxiv-2411-11888.title: Extreme events in the Liénard system with asymmetric potential: An in-depth exploration
arxiv-2411-11888.creator: B. Kaviya, R. Suresh, V. K. Chandrasekar
arxiv-2411-11888.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by B. Kaviya, R. Suresh, V. K. Chandrasekar. This research investigates the dynamics of a forced Liénard oscillator featuring asymmetric potential wells. We provide compelling evidence of extreme events (EE) in the system by manipulating the height of the potential well. In the case of a symmetric well, the system exhibits chaotic behavior, with the trajectory irregularly traversing between the two wells, resulting in frequent large oscillations under specific parameter values. However, the introduction of asymmetry in the potential wells induces a noteworthy transformation.

arxiv-2505-18632.creator: B. Ludwig, M. R. Drout, Y. Götberg, D. Lang, A. Laroche
arxiv-2505-18632.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by B. Ludwig, M. R. Drout, Y. Götberg, D. Lang, A. Laroche. Most massive stars will interact with a binary companion during their lifetimes. These interactions can remove the hydrogen-rich envelope, producing intermediate-mass ( ∼ \sim 2-8 M ⊙ \,\text{M}_{\odot} ) and helium-rich stars. These “stripped stars” are predicted to emit predominantly in the ultraviolet (UV) and can therefore be identified via a UV excess—provided they are not outshone by their companion.

arxiv-2508-09222.title: Jake D. Turner
arxiv-2508-09222.description: Abstract STUDYING EXOPLANETS IN THE RADIO FROM THE MOON Introduction : Exoplanets with and without a magnetic field are predicted to form, behave, and evolve very differently 3 . Therefore, there is great need to directly constrain these fields to holistically understand the properties of exoplanets.

arxiv-2602-10360.title: Skirting Additive Error Barriers for Private Turnstile Streams
arxiv-2602-10360.creator: Anders Aamand, Justin Y. Chen, Sandeep Silwal
arxiv-2602-10360.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Anders Aamand, Justin Y. Chen, Sandeep Silwal. We study differentially private continual release of the number of distinct items in a turnstile stream, where items may be both inserted and deleted. A recent work of Jain, Kalemaj, Raskhodnikova, Sivakumar, and Smith (NeurIPS ’23) shows that for streams of length T T , polynomial additive error of Ω ⁡ ( T 1 / 4 ) \Omega(T^{1/4}) is necessary, even without any space restrictions.

pmc-11357970.title: Cardiac tissue engineering: an emerging approach to the treatment of heart failure
pmc-11357970.creator: Hossein Rayat Pisheh, Fatemeh Sadat Nojabaei, Ahmad Darvishi, Ali Rayat Pisheh, Mahsa Sani
pmc-11357970.description: Heart failure is a major health problem in which the heart is unable to pump enough blood to meet the body’s needs. It is a progressive disease that becomes more severe over time and can be caused by a variety of factors, including heart attack, cardiomyopathy and heart valve disease.

pmc-11429985.title: Survival of hospitalised COVID-19 patients in Hawassa, Ethiopia: a cohort study
pmc-11429985.creator: Ali B. Anteneh, Marissa LeBlanc, Abebe A. Natnael, Zeytu Gashaw Asfaw
pmc-11429985.description: The COVID-19 pandemic, caused by SARS-CoV-2, led to 622,119,701 reported cases and 6,546,118 deaths. Most studies on COVID-19 patients in hospitals are from high-income countries, lacking data for developing countries such as Ethiopia.This study assesses clinical features, demographics, and risk factors for in-hospital mortality in Hawassa, Ethiopia.

pmc-11480038.title: An open-access lumbosacral spine MRI dataset with enhanced spinal nerve root structure resolution
pmc-11480038.creator: Jionghui Liu, Wenqi Zhang, Yuxing Zhou, Linhao Xu, Ying-Hua Chu, Fumin Jia
pmc-11480038.description: Spinal cord injury (SCI) profoundly affects an individual’s ability to move. Fortunately, recent advancements in neuromodulation, particularly the spatio-temporal epidural electrical stimulation (EES) targeting the spinal nerve roots, promoted rapid rehabilitation of SCI patients. Such neuromodulation techniques require precise anatomical modelling of spinal cord.

pmc-11582440.title: Effects of different slaughtering methods on the biochemical characteristics and quality changes of tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) during cold storage
pmc-11582440.creator: Xinrui Yang, Jun Mei, Jing Xie
pmc-11582440.description: Inappropriate slaughter methods can lead to differences in fish quality. In the past few years, few studies have focused on the effects of different slaughter methods on the postmortem effects of tilapia, especially the cold storage of tilapia after slaughter.

pmc-13356764.title: Thermal manipulation and heat stress: The transcriptomic landscape of the spleen in broiler chickens
pmc-13356764.creator: Mohammad Borhan Al-Zghoul, Mu’taz Almaasfeh, Shadi Shahatit, Seif Hundam, Shirin Qaaty
pmc-13356764.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Embryonic thermal manipulation (TM) has emerged as a promising strategy to enhance broiler thermotolerance, yet the transcriptional mechanisms by which it impacts immune organ responses to post-hatch thermal challenge remain poorly understood. Particularly given that heat stress (HS) compromises immune competence, suppresses lymphocyte proliferation, promotes apoptosis, and causes tissue damage, reducing organ size and functionality, leading to increased susceptibility to pathogens in heat-stressed chickens.
